exposure: Intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy with sulfadoxine and pyrimethamine (IPTp-SP) adherence and coverage
outcome: P. falciparum gene mutations (dhfr, dhps, k13)
cohort: 888 pregnant women attending 3 health facilities in Douala, Cameroon, followed from antenatal care visits to delivery.
finding: Optimal doses of IPTp-SP were associated with reduced P. falciparum infection among mothers and newborns, but had no impact on newborn bodyweight, and a high prevalence of SP-resistant P. falciparum quintuple and sextuple mutants was observed.
